text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and every change triggers automated builds. This means the software is compiled and checked without anyone doing it manually. As part of the process, the team also runs tests automatically to make sure new code does not break existing features. The main benefit is catching issues early, when they are easier and cheaper to fix. All of these steps are usually organised into CI pipelines, which guide each change from code to tested build.
